title: Eid al-Fitr
hookLine: Muslims end Ramadan with prayer, gifts and feasting; on Eid the Prophet tells Abu Bakr to let the girls sing, and zakat al-fitr feeds the poor first
tomorrow: a woman prayed so hard a priest thought she was drunk. then what?

cards: After a month of fasting, the first daytime meal is a party. Aisha, a wife of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, remembers one Eid in their home. Two girls were singing songs of an old battle.

The Prophet lay down and turned his face away. Then Abu Bakr, her father, came in and scolded them: the instruments of Satan, in the Prophet's house? The Prophet turned to him and said: leave them, Abu Bakr.
Every people has its Eid, and this is our Eid.

teach.h: THE FESTIVAL OF BREAKING THE FAST.
teach.b: Eid al-Fitr is the festival of breaking the fast, the day after Ramadan ends with the new crescent. It begins with prayer, the whole community together. And before that prayer comes a gift.

teach.h: ZAKAT AL-FITR: FOOD BEFORE THE PRAYER.
teach.b: The Prophet made zakat al-fitr a duty: a measure of food, dates or barley, given for each member of the household, young or old, before people go out to the prayer.
His cousin Ibn Abbas reports that he called it a cleansing for the one who fasted, and food for those in need. In Islam, the end of the fast isn't only a private relief.
It's a shared joy, and joy belongs to the day, as the singing girls show: this is our Eid. But no one is meant to be left outside it.

teach.h: FIRST THE GIFT, THEN THE FEAST.
teach.b: So the feast begins with food going to those who have little.
Muslims greet each other with Eid mubarak, blessed Eid, and the day is generous on purpose: new clothes, sweets, visits to family, gifts for the children. And the order matters.
First the gift and the prayer, then the feast.

how: Muslims pay zakat al-fitr, a measure of staple food or its value for each household member, before the Eid prayer; on the morning of Eid they pray together, greet each other with Eid mubarak, wear new or best clothes, visit family and share sweets.

o: the festival that breaks the month-long fast
the feast of the pilgrimage and sacrifice
the night the Qur'an was first revealed

games.q: the day of Eid: tap the pairs.
p: singing on the day of Eid
food given before the Eid prayer

s: the Prophet told Abu Bakr to stop the singing on Eid
he said: leave them; every people has its Eid, and this is our Eid.
zakat al-fitr is given before the Eid prayer
so those in need can share the feast.
Eid al-Fitr is a solemn day of fasting
it ends the fast: prayer, gifts, food and visits.

games.q: your Muslim coworker brings sweets to work on Eid and says Eid mubarak. you're not Muslim. what fits today?
o: say Eid mubarak back: the day's joy is meant to be shared.
politely decline the sweets: Eid food is only for Muslims.
say nothing about Eid; the greeting is only for Muslims.
games.why: Eid opens with food given to those in need, and the Prophet called the day's joy 'our Eid'. a returned greeting is welcome.

practice: Think of one person who'd be glad of food this week: a neighbor, a coworker, someone who's had a hard month. Decide what you'll bring them, something simple, and when. If it helps, send them a message now to say it's coming.

wordCard.voice: Eid al-Fitr: the festival of breaking the fast, begun with prayer and a gift of food so everyone can feast.

orig.note: Arabic: blessed Eid, the greeting of the day.

carryVoice: Keep this one: eid mubarak. Blessed Eid, with the food given before the feast begins. Until next time.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 952 (the two girls singing on Eid; Abu Bakr's objection; 'every people has its Eid, and this is our Eid')
Sahih al-Bukhari 1503 (zakat al-fitr: a measure of dates or barley for every Muslim, young or old, paid before people go out to the prayer)
Sunan Abu Dawud 1609 (Ibn Abbas: zakat al-fitr purifies the one who fasted and is food for the needy)
